propositions: Nested pytest child hangs after reporting 100% because pytest session cleanup synchronously scans and deletes shared user-global numbered temp trees, consuming the entire 90-second child timeout after the test itself succeeds.
The nested pytest invocation omits --basetemp argument, causing it to join pytest's user-global numbered temp root instead of using a caller-owned private basetemp.
Controlled A/B testing with 400,000 stale entries proves cleanup cost scales with retained entries: shared-root child took 10.8s while private-basetemp child took 0.882s.
The fix isolates nested pytest session-finish cleanup by passing a caller-owned tmp_path/nested-pytest via --basetemp, preserving ambient tracker state and test selection unchanged.
Real-subprocess regression test confirmed the fix: before repair, nested pytest deleted another run's sentinel file; after repair, sentinel survives and 25/25 runs pass without timeout.
